title: Pakistan | SBP Foreign Exchange, Home Remittances and Branchless Banking Operations
tagline: Apply SBP's Foreign Exchange Manual, home remittance and e-PRC rules, Branchless Banking Regulations and wire transfer information rules at a conventional bank.
description:
This quest teaches the foreign exchange, home remittance and branchless banking rules that apply to conventional banks in Pakistan. It is based on the **State Bank of Pakistan's Foreign Exchange Manual** (Chapters 2 and 10, with the basics of Chapters 12 and 13) under the **Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947**, on SBP's **Branchless Banking Regulations** (revised December 2019), and, in general terms, on the wire transfer requirements of SBP's **AML/CFT/CPF Regulations**.

Chapter 2 of the FE Manual requires every Authorized Dealer to have a board-approved foreign exchange training and development policy and to assess each related employee's FX training needs at the start of each calendar year. Officials serving individuals, including call-centre staff, must be trained; Chapter 10 asks dealers to train staff on e-PRCs; and the Branchless Banking Regulations require agent training, including for Home Remittance Accounts. This quest supports those duties for FX, remittance, branchless banking, trade and training staff and their managers.

In five stages you join a fictional Pakistani bank, from licensing to inspection readiness.

The quest builds knowledge and does not replace your bank's own foreign exchange, remittance and branchless banking policies and procedures; always follow them and the latest SBP instructions.
audience: Foreign exchange staff at authorized branches who serve individuals, sell exchange and process outward remittances
Contact and call-centre staff who answer customers' questions on foreign exchange services
Home remittance, SWIFT and payment operations staff, and branch staff who issue and verify e-PRCs
Branchless banking agent network managers, agents and branchless banking compliance staff
Trade, treasury, training and compliance managers who plan and evidence FX training for the board and SBP
outcomes: Explain how Authorized Dealers and authorized branches are licensed under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 and the FE Manual, and apply their standing duties
Serve individuals' travel, education and medical FX needs and process outward remittances with the right form, approval and checks
Credit and pay home remittances within Chapter 10's deadlines, calculate delay compensation, and issue and verify e-PRCs and S-PRCs
Run branchless banking within SBP's rules on agents, Level 0 and Level 1 accounts and Home Remittance Accounts
Keep the originator and beneficiary information SBP requires with wires and home remittances, in general terms
Build and evidence the board-approved FX training programme and annual needs assessment Chapter 2 requires

sessions.title: The FX Manual and the Authorized Dealer
sessions.summary: Learn how foreign exchange business is licensed in Pakistan: the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947, SBP's Foreign Exchange Manual and its main chapters, how a bank becomes an Authorized Dealer and designates authorized branches, and the standing duties every authorized branch carries.
objectives: Explain how the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 and SBP's Foreign Exchange Manual fit together
Describe how a bank obtains an Authorized Dealer licence and designates an authorized branch
Apply the Authorized Dealer's duties on declarations, refusal, customer notice and reporting of evasion
Use the Chapter 2 rules on returns and on the public buying and selling rate margin

cards.title: Day one at Hingol Bank
cards.setting: Foreign exchange operations floor, Hingol Bank head office, I.I. Chundrigar Road, Karachi. 9:00 am, first working day of December.

lines.text: You have just joined Hingol Bank, a fictional conventional bank with authorized branches from Gilgit to Gwadar and a branchless banking agent network, as its FX and Remittance Training Lead.

Welcome! I'm Sadia Rehman, Head of FX Operations and Home Remittances. Your first deadline is close: the foreign exchange training-needs assessment for every FX employee, due at the start of the calendar year.

Hina Javed, manager of our Lahore Gulberg branch and the FX focal person for individuals. Yesterday a new officer quoted a customer a dollar rate with a huge spread and told another that student fees 'need SBP's own approval'.
Asad Khan, trade operations, Sialkot. My exporters keep asking which rules are SBP's and which are Customs'. Half my staff can't say where the Manual even starts.
Imran Lashari, branchless banking agent network, Hyderabad. And my agents are about to start paying home remittances. Who trains them?
All of that is your mission. Five stages, from the licence vault to the inspection room. We start with the basics: who may deal in foreign exchange at all, and on what terms.

cards.title: Where Pakistan's FX rules come from

scenes.heading: The Act
scenes.narration: Pakistan's foreign exchange controls rest on the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act of 1947. Under section 3 of the Act, the State Bank may, on application, authorise a person to deal in foreign exchange.

scenes.heading: Full or limited licences
scenes.narration: SBP can allow dealing in all foreign currencies or only some, and in all kinds of transactions or only specified ones. Scheduled banks receive the licence for approved transactions of all descriptions.

scenes.heading: The Manual
scenes.narration: SBP gathers its standing instructions to Authorized Dealers in the Foreign Exchange Manual, organised in chapters, with forms and returns in the appendices. Footnotes show the circular behind each change.

scenes.heading: Authorized branches
scenes.narration: Once licensed, a bank designates the branches that will do foreign exchange business. Only those authorized branches may deal in foreign exchange.

scenes.heading: Why you are here
scenes.narration: Chapter 2 also tells Authorized Dealers to build their staff's capacity: a board-approved training policy and a yearly assessment of each related employee's FX training needs.

cards.title: The Authorized Dealer's standing duties
cards.body:
Chapter 2 sets duties that apply to every foreign exchange transaction, not just the unusual ones.

- **Stay inside the licence** (para 5). Follow SBP's general and special instructions and never deal outside the terms of the authorization.
- **Ask before you act** (para 6). Before any FX transaction, require the declarations and information that reasonably satisfy you it does not contravene or evade the Act.
- **Refuse and report** (para 6). If the person refuses or answers unsatisfactorily, refuse the transaction. If you have reason to believe a contravention is planned, report it to SBP.
- **Tell customers the rules** (para 7). Bring the FX regulations to customers' notice and apply them in daily work.
- **Report evasion immediately** (para 7). Every case of evasion, or of a direct or indirect attempt, goes to SBP as soon as it comes to notice.
- **File returns on time** (para 10) in the prescribed forms, and send senior officials to SBP meetings when called (para 8).

cards.title: SBP's powers and the dealer's duties

items.label: Licensing
items.left: May authorise all or only specified currencies and transactions
items.right: Deals only within the terms of its authorization

items.label: Refusal
items.left: May refuse a licence without assigning reasons
items.right: Must refuse a transaction when declarations are refused or unsatisfactory

items.label: Withdrawal
items.left: May withdraw a licence or stop a branch's FX dealings (s.3B)
items.right: Reports every evasion or attempted evasion to SBP immediately

items.label: Rates
items.left: Lets dealers set their own rates unless it directs otherwise
items.right: Keeps the public buy-sell margin within 50 paisa per US dollar

items.label: Returns
items.left: Prescribes return forms in the Manual's appendices
items.right: Submits returns of FX dealings on their due dates

cards.title: Two problems at the Gulberg counter
cards.setting: Hingol Bank, Gulberg branch, Lahore. 11:40 am.

lines.text: Two things before lunch. First, a walk-in customer wants USD 9,000 sent abroad for a 'relative's fees' but won't sign the declaration or show any admission letter.
He says other banks never ask, and he'll split it across three days if that helps.
And the second?
My new officer quoted retail customers a buying rate and a selling rate more than a rupee apart per dollar. He says the bank is 'free to set its rates'.
Free within limits. Let's take the customer first. Training Lead, what should Hina's team do?

cards.title: The customer who won't declare
cards.situation: A walk-in customer at an authorized branch wants to buy foreign exchange to remit abroad. He refuses to complete the declaration or give the information the branch needs, offers to split the amount over three days, and becomes impatient.

choices.text: Refuse the transaction, record what happened and refer it to the branch's compliance contact, who decides whether the facts must be reported to SBP.
choices.outcome: Right. Paragraph 6 says the dealer must refuse when declarations are refused or unsatisfactory, and report to SBP where it has reason to believe a contravention is contemplated. The offer to split also deserves an internal AML review under the bank's own procedures.

choices.text: Process the remittance today because the amount is modest and the customer is in a hurry.
choices.outcome: Poor. The size of the amount does not remove the duty to obtain declarations. Proceeding without them breaches Chapter 2 and leaves the bank exposed.

choices.text: Accept the split into three smaller remittances so that each one attracts less scrutiny.
choices.outcome: Poor. Splitting to avoid scrutiny is a warning sign in itself. Agreeing to it would help the customer evade the rules the branch is meant to apply.

choices.text: Refuse politely but keep no record, so the customer is not embarrassed.
choices.outcome: Partly right. Refusal is correct, but without a record nobody can judge whether SBP should be told or whether the pattern repeats at other branches.

cards.back: A bank licensed by SBP under the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947 to deal in foreign exchange; scheduled banks are licensed for transactions of all descriptions.
A branch the AD has designated for FX business and notified to SBP, which allots it a code for statistical reporting.

SBP Banking Services Corporation, which receives many FX returns, applications and permits on SBP's behalf.

cards.question: Hina's new officer quotes retail customers a US dollar buying rate and selling rate PKR 1.10 apart. Which statement is correct under Chapter 2?
options: It is acceptable because dealers are completely free to set their own rates
It breaches the condition that the public buy-sell margin must not exceed 50 paisa per US dollar
It is acceptable as long as the rate is displayed on the branch board
It breaches Chapter 2 only if the customer is a non-resident
cards.explanation: Paragraph 11 gives a general permission to set rates for ready and forward deals with the public, on condition that the margin between buying and selling rates does not exceed fifty paisa per US dollar or its equivalent. The condition does not apply to interbank transactions.

cards.title: Hingol case: the branch that was not on the list
cards.body:
A fictional case from Hingol Bank's files.

Hingol opened a new branch in Multan Cantt and, keen to serve families receiving money from the Gulf, the branch began buying and selling dollars in its first week. Head office had approved the plan internally but had not yet sent the branch's name and address to SBP's Statistics and Data Warehouse Department, so no reporting code had been allotted.

Internal audit spotted that the branch's FX deals were being booked through a neighbouring branch's code to make the returns balance.

**What Hingol did**
- Stopped FX dealing at the branch at once.
- Notified the branch to SBP and waited for the code before restarting.
- Corrected the returns and explained the error to SBP.
- Added 'Is this branch authorized?' to the FX induction module for every new branch team.

**Lesson:** an internal approval is not an authorization. Under Chapter 2 a branch can start FX business only after SBP has allotted its code.

cards.title: Licence Vault take-aways
items: SBP licenses Authorized Dealers under section 3 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947; scheduled banks get licences for all kinds of approved transactions.
A branch may deal in FX only after head office notifies it to SBP and receives a reporting code.
Before any FX transaction, obtain declarations; refuse if they are refused or unsatisfactory, and report planned contraventions to SBP.
Tell customers the FX rules, report every evasion or attempt immediately, and file returns on their due dates.
Dealers set their own rates, but the public buy-sell margin must stay within 50 paisa per US dollar.

cards.prompt: Think of the last foreign exchange request you handled or saw. Which declaration or document did your branch ask for, and could you explain to the customer why the Manual requires it?

quiz.question: Under which law does the State Bank of Pakistan authorise banks to deal in foreign exchange?
options: The Banking Companies Ordinance 1962
The Payment Systems and Electronic Fund Transfers Act 2007
The Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947
The Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010
quiz.explanation: Chapter 2 of the Foreign Exchange Manual says SBP authorises persons to deal in foreign exchange under section 3 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947. The other laws govern banking, payments and AML respectively.

quiz.question: A bank's head office plans to apply for an Authorized Dealer licence. To which part of SBP should the application go?
options: The Exchange Policy Department
The Statistics and Data Warehouse Department
The Financial Monitoring Unit
The Banking Policy and Regulations Department
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 2(i) directs licence applications to the Exchange Policy Department. The Statistics and Data Warehouse Department comes in later, when the bank designates authorized branches and needs reporting codes.

quiz.question: Hingol Bank wants its new Quetta branch to start selling foreign exchange next week. What must happen before the branch begins?
options: The branch manager signs an undertaking to follow the Manual
Head office notifies the branch to SBP and SBP allots it a reporting code
The branch obtains its own separate FX licence from SBP's Exchange Policy Department
The branch opens a nostro account in its own name abroad
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 2(ii) requires head office to send the new branch's name and address to SBP's Statistics and Data Warehouse Department, which allots a code for statistical reporting. Only then can the branch start FX business.

quiz.question: A customer refuses to give the information an authorized branch needs before an FX transaction, and staff suspect he plans to evade the Act. What does Chapter 2 require?
options: Complete the transaction but flag it for review next month
Refuse the transaction and simply close the file
Ask the customer to come back with a relative who will sign instead
Refuse the transaction and report the matter to SBP
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 6 requires the dealer to refuse when declarations are refused or unsatisfactory and, where it has reason to believe a contravention is planned, to report the matter to SBP. Closing the file without a report misses the second duty.

quiz.question: Which statement about the buying and selling rates an Authorized Dealer quotes to the public is correct?
options: SBP fixes a single daily rate that all dealers must quote
Dealers set their own rates with no limit on the margin
Dealers set their own rates, keeping the margin within 50 paisa per US dollar
The 50 paisa margin limit applies to interbank deals between banks but not to retail customers
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 11 gives a general permission to set rates for the public on condition that the buy-sell margin does not exceed fifty paisa per US dollar or equivalent. The condition does not apply to interbank transactions, so the last option reverses the rule.

quiz.question: A relationship officer learns that a long-standing customer attempted, through a cousin, to evade the FX regulations last week. The attempt failed. What should the bank do?
options: Nothing, because the attempt failed and no foreign exchange moved
Warn the customer privately and wait to see if it happens again
Report it in the next periodic return to SBP, together with the other exceptions of the quarter
Report the attempt to SBP immediately, because attempts must be reported too
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 7 asks Authorized Dealers to report every case of evasion or attempt, direct or indirect, immediately as it comes to notice. Failure of the attempt and indirect routing through a relative do not remove the duty.

quiz.question: Which of these may every authorized branch deal in under Chapter 2, paragraph 2(iii)?
options: Only foreign currency deposits; notes and coins need a separate licence
Only inward remittances; outward remittances and all note dealings are limited to head office
Only transactions SBP approves case by case for that branch
Foreign currency notes, drafts, letters of credit and bills payable in foreign currency
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 2(iii) permits every authorized branch to deal in foreign currency notes, coins, deposits, credits, drafts, traveller's cheques, letters of credit and bills of exchange payable in any foreign currency, reported through head office's consolidated returns.

quiz.question: A customer gives a branch a declaration he knows is false to obtain foreign exchange. Which consequence does the Manual point to?
options: The only consequence is that the bank may refuse him and charge a higher rate next time
It is a civil matter between the customer and the bank
Giving false information is an offence under section 22 of the Act
It matters only if the amount exceeds USD 10,000
quiz.explanation: Chapter 10 tells dealers to warn applicants that, under section 22 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act, giving information or making a statement known or believed to be false in a material particular is an offence. No amount threshold applies.

quiz.question: SBP-BSC calls Hingol Bank's treasury head to an urgent meeting on FX market issues. He wants to send a junior officer instead. What does Chapter 2 expect?
options: The concerned executives or senior officials attend when SBP calls them
Any staff member may attend, because SBP meetings are informal and attendance is optional
The bank may reply in writing instead of attending
Only the bank's external auditor should attend
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 8 asks banks to ensure their concerned executives or senior officials attend SBP or SBP-BSC meetings when called, so they can give feedback and the institution's stance.

quiz.question: SBP may stop an Authorized Dealer's individual branch from dealing in foreign exchange. Which power does the Manual link this to?
options: A board resolution of the Authorized Dealer
A complaint to the Banking Mohtasib
Section 22 of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act
Section 3B of the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act
quiz.explanation: Paragraph 2(iv) says SBP may refuse a licence, withdraw one already granted, or prohibit FX dealings by any authorized branch under section 3B of the Act. Section 22 concerns false statements.

cards.title: Fees, flights and a phone call
cards.setting: Hingol Bank, Gulberg branch, Lahore. Monday morning, peak admission season.

lines.text: Three customers in the queue: a father paying university fees in Manchester, a woman whose mother needs surgery in Istanbul, and a traveller off to Kuala Lumpur.
And a complaint: our contact centre told the father that fee remittances are 'only done at main branches with SBP's direct approval'. He drove two hours to get here.
Is that what Chapter 2 says about services to individuals?
No. Every authorized branch should offer travel, education and medical FX. The call centre simply didn't know.
Then this stage is about two things: the service promise to individuals, and getting outward remittances right, form by form.

scenes.heading: Cash in stock

cards.title: Outward remittances: the Chapter 10 basics
cards.body:
**What it is.** An outward remittance is any sale of foreign exchange: transfers, drafts, traveller's cheques, notes and coins (notes and coins sit in Chapter 11).

**Which form.** Every buyer lodges an application on the prescribed form with supporting documents:
- **Form I** for remittances against imports
- **Form T-1** for sale of exchange for travel
- **Form M** for all other remittances

**Who approves.** If the transaction is covered by the regulations and the dealer is empowered to approve it on SBP's behalf, the dealer may sell the exchange. If SBP's prior approval is needed, the dealer forwards the application to SBP with its comments under stamp and signature. Applicants never go to SBP directly; applications reach SBP only through a dealer.

**How to send.** Prefer telegraphic or mail transfers. Issue a draft only where normal transfer would cause real hardship, and then cross it 'Account Payee only' in the beneficiary's name.

**NRVA.** Repatriation from an NRVA needs no Form M, but is still reported under its purpose code.

cards.title: The cousin with the approval letter

lines.text: A man brings an SBP-approved Form M issued in his cousin's name for medical treatment abroad. Approval date: 41 days ago.
He wants the money sent to a different hospital account because 'the treatment moved'. The cousin is abroad and can't come in.
We see this in trade too. People think an approval is a voucher anyone can cash.
It isn't. Training Lead, how many problems can you spot in that request?

cards.title: A stale approval, a new beneficiary
cards.situation: A visitor presents an SBP-approved Form M for medical treatment issued in his cousin's name 41 days ago, with no stated longer validity and no revalidation. He asks the branch to remit to a different hospital than the one named in the approval.

choices.text: Decline to remit: the approval has lapsed, the instructions come from a third party, and the beneficiary differs. Explain revalidation and a fresh application by the applicant.
choices.outcome: Right. Approvals are valid for up to 30 days unless stated otherwise or revalidated, dealers act only for the original applicant, and they remit only to the beneficiary named in the approval. A fresh or revalidated approval is the route.

choices.text: Remit to the new hospital because the purpose, medical treatment, has not changed.
choices.outcome: Poor. The purpose may be the same, but the beneficiary is not the one approved, the instruction comes from a third party and the approval has lapsed.

choices.text: Remit to the original hospital named in the form, since that matches the approval.
choices.outcome: Partly right on the beneficiary, but still wrong: the approval has lapsed and the instruction comes from a third party, not the applicant.

choices.text: Ask the visitor to sign an indemnity and then remit as requested.
choices.outcome: Poor. An indemnity cannot cure a lapsed approval or replace the applicant's own instruction. The dealer would breach Chapter 10.

cards.back: A person who buys FX for a purpose must use it only for that purpose and meet any conditions attached.
Unused foreign exchange, or exchange whose conditions cannot be met, must be surrendered to an Authorized Dealer immediately.
Report the cancellation to SBP as an inward remittance, with a letter giving the original return date, applicant, amounts and reasons.
If the beneficiary cannot be found, report the reversal as an outward remittance on Form M with a supporting letter.
