bank.question: A bank wants an Authorized Dealer licence limited to buying and selling US dollar notes only. Which statement about SBP's powers is correct?
options: SBP can only grant a licence that covers every foreign currency and every kind of FX transaction
SBP can restrict currencies but never the type of transaction
Only the Ministry of Finance may limit a dealer's authorization
SBP may restrict an authorization to specified currencies or specified transactions
bank.explanation: Chapter 2, paragraph 1(i) lets SBP authorise dealing in all currencies or only specified ones, and all transactions or only specified ones. Scheduled banks normally receive the all-descriptions licence.

bank.question: Hingol Bank's internal committee approved FX dealing at its new Skardu branch. Treasury wants the branch to start buying dollars tomorrow, before SBP replies. What is the correct position?
options: The branch may start, because the bank's own approval is enough
The branch must wait until SBP allots its reporting code after head office notifies it
The branch may start if it books its deals through another authorized branch's code meanwhile
The branch may start but must stop if SBP objects within 30 days
bank.explanation: Under Chapter 2, paragraph 2(ii), head office notifies the branch's name and address to SBP's Statistics and Data Warehouse Department, which allots a code; the branch may start FX business thereafter. Booking through another code misreports dealings.

bank.question: During a busy day, an FX officer skips the customer declaration for a regular client because 'we know him'. Which Chapter 2 duty is breached?
options: Keeping the public buy-sell rate margin within 50 paisa per US dollar for this regular customer
Sending senior officials to SBP meetings when called
Notifying new authorized branches to SBP
Obtaining declarations and information before undertaking any FX transaction
bank.explanation: Paragraph 6 requires the dealer, before undertaking any FX transaction for any person, to obtain declarations and information that reasonably satisfy it that no contravention or evasion is involved. Familiarity with the client does not remove the duty.

bank.question: An FX officer suspects a customer intends to evade the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act and refuses the transaction. The branch manager says refusal is enough. What else does Chapter 2 expect?
options: Report the matter to SBP, since there is reason to believe a contravention is contemplated
Nothing more; refusing the transaction fully discharges the dealer's duties under Chapter 2 of the Manual
Report the customer to the Banking Mohtasib
Warn other banks by email so they also refuse him
bank.explanation: Paragraph 6 requires refusal when declarations are refused or unsatisfactory and, where the dealer has reason to believe a contravention or evasion is contemplated, a report to SBP. Paragraph 7 adds that evasion and attempts are reported immediately.

bank.question: Two banks deal with each other in the interbank market at a buying and selling spread wider than 50 paisa per US dollar. Under Chapter 2, paragraph 11, is this a breach?
options: Yes, because the margin applies to every FX deal in Pakistan
Yes, unless SBP has approved the spread in advance
No, because the 50 paisa margin condition does not apply to interbank transactions
No, because the margin applies only to forward deals
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11 lets dealers set their own ready and forward rates for the public subject to a buy-sell margin of no more than fifty paisa per US dollar, and expressly says the condition does not apply to interbank transactions.

bank.question: Which description best fits Chapter 2, paragraph 7 of the Foreign Exchange Manual?
options: Dealers file an annual summary of all customer complaints with SBP
Dealers may keep minor evasion cases internal if the amount involved is small and nothing was lost
Dealers bring FX rules to customers' notice and report every evasion or attempt immediately
Dealers report evasion only after a court has convicted the customer
bank.explanation: Paragraph 7 asks dealers to notify customers of the FX regulations, ensure compliance in day-to-day operations, and report to SBP every case of evasion or attempted evasion, direct or indirect, immediately as it comes to notice.

bank.question: An exporter asks Hingol Bank's Sialkot branch whether certifying his Form E means he no longer needs the Ministry of Commerce's export permit for a restricted item. What is the correct answer?
options: No: FX rules do not relieve exporters from export policy requirements such as permits
Yes: an Authorized Dealer's certificate replaces any export permit
Yes, provided the export proceeds will be realized through an Authorized Dealer within the prescribed period
No, but only because Form E is no longer used for any export
bank.explanation: Chapter 12, paragraph 3 says exports are regulated by the Ministry of Commerce under the Imports and Exports (Control) Act 1950, and nothing in the FX regulations relieves exporters from the Export Policy Order, including licences, permits or certificates where required.

bank.question: An importer asks Hingol Bank to approve his Electronic Import Form, but Hingol has never completed KYC/CDD on him as a customer. What does Chapter 13 expect?
options: Hingol may rely entirely on Pakistan Customs, which registers importers
Hingol may approve the EIF first and do CDD within a year
Hingol performs KYC/CDD on the importer as its customer under the applicable rules
Hingol needs no CDD because imports are regulated by the Ministry of Commerce
bank.explanation: Chapter 13 says registration of importers in WeBOC is done by Customs, but Authorized Dealers shall continue to perform KYC/CDD of importers who are their account holders, as applicable laws and regulations require.

bank.question: What role does SBP's Statistics and Data Warehouse Department play when an Authorized Dealer designates a new authorized branch?
options: It issues the bank's Authorized Dealer licence after checking its staff, systems and equipment
It sets the exchange rates the branch may quote
It receives the branch's details and allots a code for statistical reporting
It approves the branch manager's appointment
bank.explanation: Paragraph 2(ii) asks head office to send the new branch's name and address to the Statistics and Data Warehouse Department, which allots a code for statistical reporting. Licences come from the Exchange Policy Department.

bank.question: A customer at Hingol Bank's Turbat branch is told the branch cannot help with medical treatment FX and must travel to Karachi. Turbat is an authorized branch. Which duty has Hingol failed?
options: Appointing a focal person for FX services at every single authorized branch, including Turbat
Displaying exchange rates in Urdu and English
Reporting the customer's request to SBP-BSC
Offering travel, education and medical FX efficiently at all authorized branches
bank.explanation: Chapter 2, paragraph 4(i) asks dealers to offer FX services for travel, education and medical treatment efficiently at all authorized branches. The focal person is required at head office level, not at every branch.

bank.question: Where must an Authorized Dealer appoint a focal person for FX services to individuals under Chapter 2, paragraph 4(iii)?
options: At each authorized branch
At head office or principal office level
At SBP-BSC's nearest office
At the contact centre only
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4(iii) requires a focal person at head or principal office level for FX services and related matters. Branch and call-centre staff are covered by the training duty in paragraph 4(ii).

bank.question: An applicant hands his outward remittance application directly to an SBP-BSC office to save time. What will happen under Chapter 10?
options: SBP-BSC will process it, since it is the approving authority
He will be asked to resubmit it through an Authorized Dealer
SBP-BSC will forward it to any dealer of its choice
It will be approved faster because it skipped the dealer
bank.explanation: Paragraph 9 says all FX applications go to SBP or SBP-BSC through Authorized Dealers; applicants who present them directly are asked to resubmit through a dealer.

bank.question: Hingol Bank receives an SBP approval signed by an officer whose specimen signature Hingol does not hold. What should Hingol do before remitting?
options: Remit, since the embossing seal alone is sufficient
Ask the customer to confirm the officer's identity
Return the approval to the customer and ask him to obtain a fresh one signed by a known officer
Present the approval to the nearest SBP-BSC office for authentication
bank.explanation: Paragraph 11 asks dealers to check that approvals are signed by authorized SBP officers and bear the embossing seal, and to present those signed by officers whose specimen signatures they lack to the nearest SBP-BSC office for authentication.

bank.question: A traveller wants part of her approved travel exchange in notes and part in a foreign currency instrument. How should the dealer document this under Chapter 10?
options: Prepare two separate T-1 forms, each showing the amount released in that form
Use one T-1 form and note the split on the receipt
Use Form M for the foreign currency notes and Form T-1 for the instrument, filed with the same return
Use a single Form I, since both are payments abroad
bank.explanation: Paragraph 15 says that where a traveller draws exchange partly in instruments and partly in notes, the dealer prepares two separate T-1 forms and indicates on each the amounts released in instruments and in notes.

bank.question: An outward remittance reported to SBP last month is cancelled in full because the beneficiary's bank returned it. How does the dealer report the cancellation?
options: As an inward remittance, with a letter giving the original return date, applicant, amounts and reasons
By deleting the original entry from last month's return
As an outward remittance on a fresh Form M
Only in the bank's internal records, since no exchange left Pakistan
bank.explanation: Paragraph 18 requires a cancelled outward remittance to be reported as an inward remittance, supported by a letter with the date of the original return, the applicant's name and address, the original and cancelled amounts and the reasons.

bank.question: A student bought foreign exchange for tuition but the university refunded part of the fee to her. She plans to spend the refund on a holiday abroad. What does Chapter 10 require?
options: She must not use it for another purpose and should surrender it to an Authorized Dealer
She may spend it on any lawful purpose abroad
She may keep it in cash for up to a year
She may transfer it to her sibling's education abroad, since that is also an education purpose
bank.explanation: Paragraph 20 says exchange acquired for a purpose must not be used otherwise, and if it cannot be used in full or in part for that purpose it should be surrendered to an Authorized Dealer immediately.

bank.question: When effecting a remittance against an SBP permit, what must the dealer do on Form M?
options: Attach a copy of the customer's passport
State the exchange rate applied by SBP
Nothing on Form M, since a permit replaces Form M entirely for every remittance made under it
State the permit number and certify the remittance has been endorsed on the permit
bank.explanation: Paragraph 13 requires dealers to report permit remittances on Form M, stating the permit number and certifying that the remittance has been endorsed on the permit, which itself is endorsed with amount and date under stamp and signature.

bank.question: A home remittance for a beneficiary at another bank reaches Hingol at 10 am Monday. Hingol passes the credit at 10 am Wednesday, and the other bank credits at once. How many days of delay compensation are owed?
options: One day, because the 24-hour window ended at 10 am Tuesday
None, because the other bank credited instantly
Two days, counting from receipt on Monday
Three days, because Monday is included in full
bank.explanation: Chapter 10 allows the recipient bank at most 24 hours from receipt to pass the credit on. That window closed at 10 am Tuesday, so the credit on Wednesday morning was about one day late and the 65 paisa per thousand per day return applies.

bank.question: A home remittance of PKR 250,000 is paid two days late. What compensation is due under Chapter 10?
options: PKR 325
PKR 650
bank.explanation: At 65 paisa per thousand rupees per day: 250 thousands x 0.65 x 2 days = PKR 325. PKR 162.50 is one day, and PKR 650 doubles the result.

bank.question: Hingol Bank's remittance partner insists its standard contract need not go to SBP because 'SBP will be responsible if anything goes wrong'. What is correct?
options: SBP approves the contract, after which SBP becomes responsible for its terms and any losses
Send the draft to SBP for input; Hingol stays responsible for protecting its own interest
The contract need not go to SBP if the partner is foreign
Only agreements with banks inside Pakistan go to SBP
bank.explanation: Chapter 10, paragraph 3 requires drafts of all home remittance agreements with entities inside and outside Pakistan to go to the Exchange Policy Department before finalising. SBP may comment, but the ultimate responsibility remains with the bank.

bank.question: A complaint says a cash-over-the-counter home remittance was 'not ready' when the beneficiary arrived the day after the funds reached the bank. What standard applies?
options: Cash payouts may take up to 24 hours
Funds offered as cash over the counter must be available instantly
Cash payouts may take up to three working days
Cash payouts have no time standard in Chapter 10
bank.explanation: Paragraph 4(i)(d) says that where banks offer cash over the counter to beneficiaries, they must ensure the funds are available instantly.

bank.question: What is a Proceeds Realization Certificate, according to the e-PRC guidelines?
options: A licence allowing a customer to receive remittances
A tax certificate issued by FBR on foreign income
A SWIFT message from the correspondent bank confirming that a payment was sent to Pakistan
Documentary proof that funds received from abroad were realized in Pakistan
bank.explanation: The guidelines describe the PRC as documentary proof of funds received from abroad and realized in Pakistan, for example workers' remittances, export proceeds, equity or loans.

bank.question: In the different bank model, Bank B cannot issue an accurate e-PRC because Bank A sent only the amount and the beneficiary's account number. Which bank failed its duty?
options: Bank B, which should have issued the e-PRC on whatever partial data it received, and asked later
Neither bank, because e-PRCs are optional in that model
Bank A, which must send complete transaction information in the standard MT102/MT103 format
The overseas correspondent, which must issue the e-PRC
bank.explanation: Under the different bank model the recipient or intermediary bank must send the amount with complete information as per the MT102 and MT103 formats; the beneficiary's bank issues the e-PRC based on that complete information.

bank.question: A Hingol branch still issues every e-PRC in duplicate 'as Chapter 12 requires'. What is the current position?
options: Duplicates are still required for export proceeds only, under Chapter 12's own paragraph
Duplicates are required for amounts above USD 1,000
The duplicate e-PRC requirement, including under Chapter 12, has been withdrawn
Duplicates are now required in triplicate for exports
bank.explanation: The guidelines state that the requirement to issue e-PRCs in duplicate under SBP instructions, including Chapter 12, paragraph 31, stands withdrawn, to realign with the automated issuance process.

bank.question: Hingol Bank changes the focal person who handles e-PRC verification queries. What do the guidelines expect?
options: Inform SBP's Statistics and Data Warehouse Department only
Publish the change in a national newspaper
No action, since verifying agencies contact branches directly
Inform the relevant verifying agencies of the change
bank.explanation: The guidelines ask dealers to inform relevant verifying agencies when their focal person changes or when their online verification user manual is modified, and to share focal person contact details.

bank.question: Which statement about Chapter 10's treatment of inward remittances is correct?
options: Inward remittances above a set amount need SBP's prior approval before the dealer can buy them
There is no restriction on receiving remittances from abroad in foreign currency
Only remittances from Gulf countries are freely allowed
Inward remittances must be converted to rupees within a week
bank.explanation: Paragraph 2 says there is no restriction on receipt of remittances from abroad, in foreign currency or by debit to non-resident rupee accounts of banks' overseas branches or correspondents, and dealers may freely purchase them.

bank.question: In every branchless banking model, where must the customer's money actually sit?
options: On the telecom partner's server as stored value, which the bank settles at the end of each day
In the agent's float account until withdrawn
In the customer's account at the bank; balances on the phone only mirror it
On the customer's SIM card as electronic money
bank.explanation: Section 3.1(e) requires the customer relationship to reside with a bank, every transaction to hit the actual account, and no monetary value to be stored on the phone or provider's server. Banks must directly own the branchless banking platform.

bank.question: A customer's son asks an agent to open a Level 1 account in his father's name and to operate it for him because the father is unwell. What do the Regulations allow?
options: Both, if the son produces his own CNIC
Opening only, provided the father later signs
Neither: accounts cannot be opened for, or operated on behalf of, another individual
Operation only, provided the father opened the account himself and gave the son a written mandate
bank.explanation: Section 4.2(b)(iii) bars banks from opening branchless banking accounts on behalf of other individuals and from allowing anyone to operate an account on the holder's behalf.

bank.question: A small trading company asks to open a branchless banking account for its petty cash. What is the rule?
options: Allowed as Level 0, with a lower limit
Allowed as a Level 1 account after biometric verification of the company's managing director
Allowed if the company is not high risk
Branchless banking accounts are for individuals only, not legal persons or arrangements
bank.explanation: Section 4.2(b)(i) says branchless banking accounts are for individuals only and shall not be opened for legal persons or arrangements, or for high-risk customers and geographies the bank identifies.

bank.question: A Level 0 account holder has received Rs. 45,000 this month and wants to receive Rs. 10,000 more. What does section 4.3 indicate?
options: It exceeds the Rs. 50,000 monthly limit, which applies separately to receipts
It is fine because limits apply only to payments
It is fine because the yearly limit is Rs. 200,000
It exceeds the Rs. 25,000 monthly limit for Level 0
bank.explanation: Level 0 accounts have limits of Rs. 25,000 per day, Rs. 50,000 per month and Rs. 200,000 per year, treated separately for payments and receipts. Receipts of Rs. 55,000 in a month would exceed the monthly limit.

bank.question: When must a bank not apply simplified due diligence to branchless banking customers under section 4.2?
options: When the customer opens the account remotely
When the customer is a first-time account holder who has never had a bank account before
When ML/TF is suspected or higher-risk factors or jurisdictions are identified
When the account is opened at an agent location
bank.explanation: Section 4.2(a) rules out simplified due diligence where there is a suspicion of ML/TF, where high-risk factors are identified by SBP, the bank or international standards, and for customers from jurisdictions with inadequate AML/CFT measures.

bank.question: A customer cannot complete CDD at the time of a branchless banking transaction, and the bank believes pursuing CDD would tip off a suspected launderer. What does section 4.2 direct?
options: Complete the transaction and finish CDD next month
Stop pursuing CDD and file a suspicious transaction report instead
Ask the agent to complete CDD at the counter
Close the account quietly with no report
bank.explanation: Section 4.2(b)(xiii) says that where the bank suspects ML/TF and reasonably believes CDD would tip off the customer, it shall not pursue CDD and shall file an STR instead.

bank.question: An existing wallet holder registers for a Home Remittance Account through the mobile app. When may she make her first withdrawal from it?
options: After a one-time in-person visit to a nearby agent completes registration
Immediately, because the app verified her PIN
After 30 days, once the first remittance clears
Only at a bank branch, never at an agent
bank.explanation: Annexure A paragraph 16 requires remote registrants to visit a nearby agent once for face-to-face contact and cash withdrawal, and allows no debit before registration is complete.

bank.question: Who bears the cost of NADRA biometric verification when an HRA is opened?
options: The bank; the cost should not be passed on to the customer
The customer, deducted from the first remittance
The agent, from the commission earned
The overseas remitter, through a fee
bank.explanation: Annexure A paragraph 7 requires NADRA biometric verification at opening to activate the HRA instantly and says its cost should not be passed on to the customer, to encourage remittance inflows.

bank.question: Hingol Bank's agent contracts say nothing about who answers to customers for agents' mistakes. What does section 9.1 require customer agreements to state?
options: The agent is solely responsible for its own errors
Responsibility is shared equally by the bank and the agent under the standard agency agreement
The bank is responsible to the customer for the agent's acts of omission and commission
The telecom partner is responsible for agent errors
bank.explanation: Section 9.1(b) requires all customer agreements to state clearly that the bank is responsible to the customer for the agent's acts of omission and commission.

bank.question: Hingol Bank sends a cross-border wire for a customer. Which record must it keep under Regulation 11(2)?
options: Only the amount and the beneficiary's account number, since the SWIFT system keeps everything else
Details allowing reconstruction, such as date, currency, amount, value date, purpose and beneficiary
Only the SWIFT confirmation from the correspondent
Nothing beyond the customer's signed instruction
bank.explanation: As ordering institution, the bank identifies and verifies the originator and records adequate details to reconstruct the wire: date, currency type and amount, value date, purpose, beneficiary and beneficiary institution details and, where applicable, the parties' relationship.

bank.question: A respondent bank abroad repeatedly sends wires to Hingol without originator information despite requests. What does Regulation 11(7) direct?
options: Limit or prohibit relationships or transactions with that institution
Continue as normal, since the duty lies only with the sender
Ask each beneficiary to obtain the details from the sender
Report the respondent to the Banking Mohtasib
bank.explanation: Regulation 11(7) requires SBP-regulated entities to limit or prohibit relationships or transactions with institutions that do not comply with the standard requirements for wire transfers.

bank.question: A Gulf money transfer company batches 300 individual remittances from one originator into one file to Hingol's branchless banking accounts. What must the batch contain?
options: Only a total amount and a count of beneficiaries
Only the beneficiaries' mobile numbers
Originator details only for amounts above USD 1,000, and a single total for the rest of the batch
Accurate originator information and full beneficiary information that is traceable
bank.explanation: Section 5(f) of the Branchless Banking Regulations, mirroring Regulation 11(4), requires batch files from a single originator to contain the required and accurate originator information and full, traceable beneficiary information.

bank.question: Chapter 2, paragraph 3(ii) asks dealers to identify training focus areas. When and on what basis?
options: After each SBP inspection, based only on the findings in the latest inspection report
Every three years, based on staff preferences
At year end, based on the training budget left
Before the start of each calendar year, keeping in view the risks of different areas
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3(ii) says focus areas such as international trade, foreign currency accounts, remittances and inward or outward investments may be identified before the start of each calendar year, keeping in view the risks in each area.

bank.question: Hingol Bank's FX staff complete courses, but nobody checks what they learned. Which element of Chapter 2, paragraph 3 is missing?
options: A board-approved training and development policy
A suitable mechanism to assess employees' performance after training
Coordination with IBP, NIBAF and universities
Function-specific FX training counted in career growth
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3(vi) encourages in-house trainers and asks dealers to chalk out a suitable mechanism to assess employee performance after training. The other elements may exist without any assessment of learning.

bank.question: Which institutions does Chapter 2, paragraph 3(vii) name for coordination on designing FX courses?
options: The FMU, NACTA and the Ministry of Interior
IBP, NIBAF and local business schools or universities, directly or through PBA
SECP, FBR and the Banking Mohtasib
Only SBP's own training academy
bank.explanation: Paragraph 3(vii) asks dealers to enhance coordination with the Institute of Bankers Pakistan, the National Institute of Banking and Finance and local business schools or universities, directly or through the Pakistan Banks' Association.

bank.question: An SBP inspector reviewing Hingol's branchless banking asks how ML/TF risks are assessed each year. What do the Regulations require?
options: A one-time assessment at the time SBP authorized the service
A yearly risk matrix of threats, vulnerabilities, controls and residual risk, informed by the national risk assessment
An assessment only when the FMU raises a concern
An assessment carried out by the agents themselves
bank.explanation: Section 4.1(b) requires banks to build a risk matrix covering threats, vulnerabilities, control effectiveness and residual risk, conducted yearly in light of the national ML/TF risk assessment and the overall risk profile of branchless banking.

bank.question: Hingol's training plan for the year covers branch FX staff but leaves out branchless banking agents and contact-centre staff. Which two provisions does this most clearly fall short of?
options: AML/CFT/CPF Regulation 11 and Chapter 10, paragraph 6
Chapter 12, paragraph 3 and Chapter 13, paragraph 2
BB Regulations section 9(b) on agent capacity building and FX Manual Chapter 2, para 4(ii)
BB Regulations section 4.4 on domestic transfers and FX Manual Chapter 2, paragraph 11 on rates
bank.explanation: Section 9(b) asks banks to build agents' capacity through training, especially on ML/TF risks, and Chapter 2, paragraph 4(ii) expressly includes contact and call-centre staff among those to be trained in FX business.
